claims: Revenue is the total amount of money a business generates from the sale of goods or services.
Revenue is the total amount of money a government collects.
Revenue is often referred to as the "top line".
Revenue is calculated as Units Sold × Average Price.
Revenue is recorded on the income statement before subtracting expenses.
Operating revenue is income from core business operations.
Non-operating revenue is income from peripheral sources.
Gross revenue is the total received.
Net revenue subtracts returns, allowances, and discounts.
The basic formula for revenue is Revenue = Number of Units Sold × Price per Unit.
Sales revenue is cash or accounts receivable generated from selling goods or services.
Interest/investment income is revenue from holding interest-bearing assets.
Royalties/licensing is income from allowing others to use intellectual property.
Under accrual basis, revenue is recognized when earned, not necessarily when cash is received.
Under cash basis, revenue is recognized only when cash is actually received.
Revenue recognition requires that it must be earned (goods delivered or services rendered) and realizable (payment expected).
Revenue is a top-line metric.
Revenue per employee is a metric used to evaluate productivity.
Price-to-sales (P/S) is a ratio used to value companies that are not yet profitable.
Government revenue consists of funds collected to pay for public expenditures.
Government revenue is primarily collected through taxes (income tax, sales tax, corporate tax), fines, and licensing fees.
